items.headline: WHO Emergency Committee meets for fifth time as reproduction number tops 1.3
items.summary: The World Health Organization convened its Emergency Committee for the fifth time today as new modelling data placed the effective reproduction number at 1.31, surpassing the 1.25 containment threshold set in March. The committee is expected to issue updated guidance on border measures and resource allocation within 48 hours.

items.headline: Khartoum field hospitals reach operational capacity three days after deployment
items.summary: Emergency field hospitals deployed to Khartoum following last week's system overload declaration have already reached operational capacity, according to MSF officials on the ground. The organisation is requesting additional medical personnel from the WHO Emergency Operations Centre and bilateral response partners.

items.headline: Phase II vaccine trial in Cairo expands to second site
items.summary: The lead vaccine candidate's Phase II clinical trial has expanded from its original Cairo site to a second trial centre following strong initial safety data. The trial now includes 840 participants. Results are expected within 90 days, which would allow an accelerated Phase III programme if safety benchmarks are met.

items.headline: Nairobi cluster contained; airport enhanced screening extended to four additional hubs
items.summary: Kenyan health authorities have confirmed containment of the Nairobi transit hub cluster after no new cases emerged in the past 12 days. The ECDC has recommended that the enhanced traveller screening protocol currently in place at four African hubs be extended to five additional airports with high-volume connections to affected regions.

items.headline: ProMED report flags unusual respiratory presentation in Aden cluster
items.summary: A new ProMED post flags an unusual respiratory presentation in three of the 28 confirmed Aden cases — distinct from the predominant clinical profile seen elsewhere. Field investigators are collecting additional samples. WHO has dispatched a rapid characterisation team and results are expected within 72 hours.

items.headline: G7 health ministers agree emergency resource package for affected nations
items.summary: G7 health ministers agreed in principle to a coordinated emergency package covering PPE, diagnostic capacity, and logistical support for the five most-affected nations. The package — valued at approximately USD 340 million — is subject to parliamentary approval in three member states and is expected to begin disbursement within four weeks.

items.headline: Egypt reports first sustained transmission outside Cairo; Delta region under elevated watch
items.summary: Egyptian health authorities have confirmed a secondary transmission chain in the Nile Delta region, marking the first confirmed sustained spread outside the Cairo metropolitan area. The US CDC updated its Egypt travel advisory to Level 3 and issued interim clinical guidance for clinicians seeing patients with recent Egypt travel history.

items.headline: Addis Ababa genomic data confirms single importation event; no divergent strains
items.summary: Whole-genome sequencing of the Addis Ababa cluster confirms all 620 cases derive from a single importation event in February, with no divergent sublineages detected. This is considered reassuring by WHO technical staff, who note it suggests the outbreak remains a single-origin event without significant in-country evolution.
